newsitem.title: CHINA: Salomons issues buy rating for Singapore Airlines.
newsitem.headline: Salomons issues buy rating for Singapore Airlines.

text.p: Salomon Brothers has revised its 1998 profit estimate for Singapore Airlines (SIA) and upgraded its share recommendation to "buy".

An aviation research report from the investment bankers dated July 22 said "robust" earnings growth is expected in 1998, driven largely by external factors such as a more stable currency environment, lower fuel prices and increased gains from aircraft sales.

Salomon raised its forecast of SIA's 1998 profits by 7.4 percent to S$1,171.9 million from S$1,091 million to reflect the better than expected operating environment for the airline. Salomon said it had also initiated a 1999 profit estimate of S$1,182 million.
"SIA maintains the strongest financial position of any listed global carrier," the report said.

Asia's currency crises may slow regional traffic but a stronger yen should provide relief. Salomons also said it is optimistic for the potential of SIA's new alliance with Ansett Australia and Air New Zealand.

The report said Salomons has raised its year end target to S$16.50 for the foreign stock from its last published target in April of S$14.25, and a stock price of S$13.3 on July 22, giving a 24 per cent upside potential.
On load factors and yields, the report said passenger and cargo load factors should hold steady "which will be a solid result considering the increase in capacity."
Strong intra-regional cargo traffic growth should support the company's capacity investment, the report added.
